items.title: File Clackamas County business personal property return
items.description: Oregon businesses file a Confidential Personal Property Return with the county assessor by March 15 (March 16 when the 15th falls on a weekend) for taxable personal property held on January 1; returns filed after the deadline pay 5% of the tax through June 1, 25% through August 1 and 50% after (ORS 308.296). Returns can be filed electronically through eNoticesOnline.

items.title: File the TriMet transit payroll tax with the Oregon Quarterly Tax Report
items.description: Employers with payroll in the TriMet district (parts of Multnomah, Washington and Clackamas counties) report and pay the transit payroll tax on Form OQ each quarter, due April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 (next business day if a weekend or holiday). The rate is set each year (0.8037% in 2023); a late payment adds 5%.

items.title: Withhold the Metro Supportive Housing Services income tax for high earners
items.authority: Metro / City of Portland Revenue Division
items.description: Employers offer withholding of Metro's 1% supportive housing services tax on income above $125,000 (individuals) or $200,000 (joint), with payment due on the same dates as federal and Oregon withholding deposits. Reported separately from other local taxes. Applies to workers in the Metro district (Multnomah, Washington and Clackamas counties).

items.title: File Lane County business personal property return

The 2026 deadline was March 16; free drop-in help is offered at the Eugene office.

items.title: File Marion County business personal property return
items.description: Oregon business personal property returns are due to the county assessor by March 15 each year; late returns incur penalties of 5%, 25% and 50%.

items.title: File Multnomah County business personal property return
items.description: Oregon business personal property returns are due to the county assessor by March 15 each year; late returns incur penalties of 5%, 25% and 50%. Returns are filed on Form OR-CPPR by email, mail or the county's Smartfile portal.

items.title: Withhold the Multnomah County Preschool for All tax from high earners
items.authority: Multnomah County / City of Portland Revenue Division
items.description: Employers with a Multnomah County location withhold the Preschool for All personal income tax (1.5% above $125,000 or $200,000 joint, and more above $250,000 or $400,000; rates rise in 2026) from employees who work in the county and earn $200,000 or more in the year. It has its own withholding return remitted to the City of Portland.
